summary: Defines a new WebDAV property that lets a client quickly find the principal that corresponds to the currently authenticated user. This is a Proposed Standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This WebDAV extension adds a property that identifies the principal associated with the current authenticated user. A client can use the principal's URL to ask for more information about that user.

questions: how to find the current user in webdav
how does webdav identify the current user
subtitle: A WebDAV property that identifies the principal for the authenticated user.

tldr.problem: WebDAV access-control clients needed a direct way to identify the principal linked to the current authenticated user.
tldr.mechanism: The DAV:current-user-principal property returns one URL to the user's principal resource or a DAV:unauthenticated element.
tldr.outcome: A client can use the returned principal URL to make further queries about that user.

today: RFC 5397 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Finding the Current User's Principal
sections.content:
WebDAV ACL represents authenticated entities with principal resources. A client may need to find the principal associated with its current HTTP user, for example to ask about group membership or change a property on that principal. Earlier mechanisms did not provide a recommended direct way to identify the individual principal.

RFC 5397 adds the DAV:current-user-principal property to resources under access control so a client can locate a principal resource and make further queries.
sections.plainLanguage: A WebDAV client may need to know which principal represents its logged-in user. This property gives the client a direct way to find that principal.

sections.title: The Property's Value
sections.content:
The protected property is computed for each request and contains one DAV:href or DAV:unauthenticated element. The href must be an HTTP or HTTPS URL listed in the principal resource's DAV:principal-URL or DAV:alternate-URI-set property. If authentication has not occurred or has failed, the value must be DAV:unauthenticated.

If several principal resource URLs correspond to the same authenticated principal, the server may choose any one, but should use the same URL consistently. The property is not copied or moved.
sections.plainLanguage: For a logged-in user, the property gives one web address for the user's principal. If there is no successful authentication, it reports that the user is unauthenticated.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says this extension introduces no additional security issues beyond those defined for HTTP, WebDAV and WebDAV ACL. The property is protected and computed per request.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension adds no security issues beyond those already covered by HTTP and WebDAV access control. The server computes the property for each request.
